title: Division Expressions with Fractions and Mixed Numbers
objective: I can explain what dividing a fraction by a fraction means, find the quotient with common denominators or by multiplying by the reciprocal, and check it by multiplying.
model: bar cut into common-denominator pieces: how many copies of the divisor fit in the dividend (then the reciprocal shortcut, checked by multiplying)

widgets.root: Exactly the lesson's warm-up (6-1 content as review); 12, 18, 15, 40 are right and the wrong choices name dividing by the denominator or adding.

widgets.component: First Half: reciprocal of 3/5, 1/2 ÷ 1/4, 3/4 ÷ 1/8, first step for 2 1/2 ÷ 1/4, 2/3 ÷ 1/3
widgets.root: Reciprocal and mixed-number→improper-fraction are in this lesson's objective and key idea; recomputed 2, 6, 2 and the improper-fraction first step. Wrong-answer feedback gives the common-denominator check (6/8 ÷ 1/8) but the hint ladders on 2.2, 2.3, 2.5 open with the keep-change-flip mnemonic before the bar/common-denominator reasoning the objective asks for first.

widgets.component: Spot the Common Mistake: '1/2 ÷ 1/4, divide straight across = (1 ÷ 1)/(2 ÷ 4) = 1/(1/2) = 2'
widgets.root: The student's work is a valid method (a/b ÷ c/d = (a ÷ c)/(b ÷ d)) and the answer 2 is correct, yet the item marks the step wrong and the fix says straight-across division 'is not how fraction division works' and 'falls apart on 2/3 ÷ 1/2'; (2 ÷ 1)/(3 ÷ 2) = 2/(3/2) = 4/3, which is right. The item teaches a false statement.
widgets.replacement: Replace the card with a real error on 3/4 ÷ 1/8: Step 'Divide the top numbers and keep the bottom': (3 ÷ 1)/4 = 3/4, answer 3/4 pound (e = the step that keeps the denominator). Fix: 'Renaming 3/4 as 6/8 shows 6 eighths ÷ 1 eighth = 6; dividing only the numerators ignores that the pieces are different sizes.' Delete the sentence about straight-across division.

widgets.component: Second Half: sort six quotients, 2/3 cup with a 1/6 scoop, forgot-to-flip error, full evidence bag weight, rate per hour
widgets.root: Recomputed all (2, 2, 2.5, 4, 3.5, 2/3 into bins; 4 scoops; 1/2 pound; 4/5 box); the 3.3 error (changed ÷ to × without flipping) is a real misconception named at the right step.

widgets.component: Generated reciprocal, 'which question does a/b ÷ c/d ask', fraction ÷ fraction, mixed-number rewrite to improper fractions, ribbon pieces
widgets.root: Checked 60 seeds per level: quotients exact (3/10 ÷ 3/4 = 2/5, 1 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = 2), distractors are named slips (multiplied, unflipped, reciprocal of the wrong number). Mixed-number conversion is part of this lesson's title and worked example, though 6-10 re-teaches it.

widgets.component: Cut the bars with a mixed-number dividend and a proper-fraction divisor
widgets.root: Same manipulable model as 6-1 with the divisor now a non-unit fraction; pieces per bar must be a common multiple of both denominators, so the common-denominator idea is the interaction. Sampled 12 seeds: 1 2/3 ÷ 1/3 … 3 1/2 ÷ 1/4, all exact.

widgets.component: Final Whistle: 5/6 ÷ 1/12, rewrite 5/6 as twelfths, 5/6 ÷ 1/12 again
widgets.root: Mathematics right (10, 10/12). 5.4 is the exit ticket and repeats the stem of 5.1 word for word, so the section checks one skill twice.

widgets.component: If each piece were 1/6 of a foot, how many pieces?
widgets.root: Connect.check item 3 lifted without the scenario (a carpenter's 5/6-foot board cut into 1/12-foot pieces) or its tape diagram; the stem has no board, so 5 cannot be derived.
widgets.replacement: Carry cfg.connect.scenario and cfg.connect.diagram into mastery items (practice-studio-config.mjs buildSections), or rewrite: 'A carpenter cuts a 5/6-foot board into pieces. If each piece is 1/6 foot instead of 1/12 foot, how many pieces?' (key 5) with the tape diagram 'Board Cut Into 1/12-ft Pieces'. Also replace 5.4 (duplicate of 5.1) with 'Which multiplication checks 5/6 ÷ 1/12 = 10?' (key 10 × 1/12 = 5/6).

widgets.component: Climb the ladder: fraction ÷ fraction, ribbon/yard/part-whole, nested (a ÷ b) ÷ c, missing dividend/divisor
widgets.root: Checked 54-60 seeds per level: answers exact, part-to-whole stems ('1/3 mile is 2/3 of the race' → 1/2) reuse the divide-to-find-the-whole meaning from 6-1; L4 missing-number items are solved by the lesson's own check-by-multiplying.

widgets.component: Playbook: error card, paint fields, relay legs, cooler table, miles per hour
widgets.root: Recomputed 4 fields from 3 1/2 ÷ 3/4, 6 legs, cooler table (10, 4, 2) and 4 miles; the table is numeric so 5/2 or 2 1/2 both grade. The err card (multiplied by 3/4 instead of 4/3) is a real slip at the right step.

widgets.where: Challenge §3 items 3.1-3.3 (act:barcut mixed L3, L4; match)
widgets.component: Cut the bars with leftover pieces counted as part of a group; pick the division sentence; match four divisions
widgets.root: L3 forces a leftover part-group (2 1/3 ÷ 3/4 = 3 1/9) and L4 reverses the task; all quotients exact on 12 seeds each. Match pairs 6, 14, 2, 4 1/2 are right.

widgets.component: Replay Detective: flipped the dividend, kept the whole number of a mixed number, changed only the sign, and 'dividing makes it smaller'
widgets.root: Each error is at the named step (Flip, Multiply, Change) and each is a real slip for this lesson; 4.4 correctly resolves 3/4 ÷ 1/8 > 1.

widgets.component: Championship Boss: rope pieces, quotient > 1, bottles, check by multiplying, drills
Compare 3/4 ÷ 1/2 with 1/2 ÷ 3/4; create your own problem
widgets.root: Passes on 40 characters and self-ticked rubric lines, model answer shown immediately, no check that the two quotients were computed.
widgets.replacement: Require two numeric boxes (3/4 ÷ 1/2 and 1/2 ÷ 3/4) graded by value before the explanation box unlocks, then ask 'Does order matter? Yes/No' with three reasons to choose from; show the model answer after both.

formulaOrder.formula: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c (reciprocal) and mixed number → improper fraction
